<reason>CON won a close, high-quality clash by giving the cleaner decision rule: a timed “realistic” markdown or donation duty uniquely distorts the first-price aisle through waiting, extra handling, earlier culls, and thinner everyday range, while pricing disposal can tax waste without commandeering the shopping channel. PRO’s private-vs-social and transfer arguments were theoretically sharp and well bounded, but they never showed those gains dominate the distortions or that records and inspections can stop preemptive unsaleable labeling.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s R2 reply that a markdown can be a transfer while the mandate still creates net loss via handling, postponed demand, and missing regular stock, and that a dumpster charge does not order a second market in the aisle.</best_rebuttal>
